content_of_post_to_comment: You're against AI. You're against the rich. You're against Trump. You're against fascism. You're against Israel. Every week there's something new to be "against"; isn't that exciting? Always a heretic to be ousted, a crusade to go on, a problem that needs your focused, directed, seething rage. And year after year passes, and the problem changes, but the results never do—there is always someone new to hate. This is such providence. You are so lucky! If you could stop focusing on all the things you're "against," you might for a minute see that there are things to be grateful for. You might identify problems in your own life that can actually be solved, with careful attention, and love, and gratitude, instead of foot-stomping blistering outrage. You might discover that your anger is worse than useless; it's actively keeping you from becoming the best version of yourself that you could be. You might find that there are many more things to be happy about than to be angry about, that to be "against" something means that really, you stand for nothing, and the reason that you always have to be "against" something new is that you have no real stronghold, nothing of worth, to actually defend against. You might have it revealed to you that without joy, without a thing to fight FOR, you are fighting while standing in quicksand, a land eager to swallow you and leave nothing. Because you too, are also eager to be nothing. But that would be difficult. And you might fail. So how about you just forget all that, and tell me again, how much you hate AI.
comment: A useful distinction might be between anger as a signal and anger as an identity. The first can reveal what needs attention; the second can become a substitute for actually building anything.
